title: Temperaments
description: Systems that tune or identify ratios by tempering small differences.

title.label: Title
title.heading: Temperaments
title.body: A temperament intentionally treats certain small ratio differences, called commas, as negligible. This lets a tuning system simplify just-intonation relationships into practical mappings and repeatable musical patterns.

prerequisites.label: Just Intonation
prerequisites.body: Temperaments start from ratio relationships and decide which differences to merge.

relatedConcepts.label: Equal Tuning
relatedConcepts.body: Equal tunings can realize temperament mappings in concrete step systems.

relatedConcepts.label: Moments of Symmetry
relatedConcepts.body: Temperaments often produce useful generated and MOS scale patterns.

qa.label: Q&A
qa.question: What does tempering a comma usually mean?

choices.text: Treating a small ratio difference as equivalent or negligible.
Forcing every chord to use one pitch.

items.title: Find a simplification
items.body: Write one musical reason a composer might want to merge two very close ratio paths.

items.title: Relate to an EDO
items.body: Choose an equal tuning and describe how it might approximate a family of ratios.
